title: Portal 5 — Orchestrated Worker Usage & Cost
description: Plan quota, seat roster, token usage and cost for the Claude Code orchestration layer. Seats are grouped by model family so the same model bought from two providers reads as one stack, and retired seats keep their history in a collapsed row rather than cluttering the current roster. Quota is the vendor's own reading: Z.ai Coding Plan pools and an Alibaba TP credit pool, Claude Pro, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenCode Go, Gemini Pro through `agy -p /usage`, DeepSeek and Moonshot balances, and OrcaRouter's wallet plus its free-package ladder. MiMo publishes no balance endpoint, so its figure is derived; Codex/Grok headline plans are flat-rate and appear in spend as well as in their own utilisation.

panels.title: Seats — who can be picked, and how they have done
Current seats — one row per routable seat, grouped by family
panels.description: Every seat `auto` or an explicit `--tier` can still pick, sorted so one model family reads as one stack across providers. `Status` is how the seat is reached: auto (the router may choose it) or explicit (only on request). Runs, accepted and judged are lifetime totals from the dispatcher registry, so `Accept %` compares like with like; it is blank until a seat has a verdict, which is the honest reading: no evidence. `Last used` and the token/cash columns answer what is in use now, and none of these depend on Prometheus history, so they survive a Prometheus restart.

targets.expr: ((100 * sum by (seat) (orchestrate_seat_accepted) / clamp_min(sum by (seat) (orchestrate_seat_judged), 1)) and on(seat) (sum by (seat) (orchestrate_seat_judged) > 0)) * on(seat) group_left(family,provider,plan,harness,role,status) orchestrate_seat_info{status=~"auto|explicit"}

panels.title: Family × kind — what auto routes on
panels.description: Accepted and judged dispatches pooled by model family and task kind. Routing ranks a family per kind, so this is the evidence behind a choice; a cell with one or two judged runs is noise, not a finding. Families are the model, not the provider — the same family bought twice pools here.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (family, kind) (orchestrate_family_kind_accepted) / clamp_min(sum by (family, kind) (orchestrate_family_kind_judged), 1)

panels.title: Provider reliability — failures by seat and reason
panels.description: Every failed dispatch recorded for a seat, split by why it failed: the harness crashed, the run stalled, the provider rate-limited, or it refused on quota — the four reason columns sum to the seat's failed dispatches. Counts are lifetime (the registry keeps them), so `Failure %` is against lifetime runs. A rate limit or quota refusal is the provider telling the truth late — the seat was picked when its plan had no headroom; a stall or harness error is the model or the wrapper.

panels.title: Retired seats — history only, never routable
panels.description: Seats and models that are no longer in the roster (removed, or retired at a known date) but still have recorded dispatches. They are kept so a verdict and its cost stay attributable after the seat is gone; nothing here can be picked by auto or by an explicit --tier. `Last used` is the last dispatch the registry recorded, not the model's deprecation date.

panels.title: Plan headroom — switch before a plan blocks
Plan headroom and resets — every plan that publishes a quota
panels.description: One row per prepaid plan window, soonest refill first. Left % is the vendor's own reading (red under 15, amber under 40); 'Resets at' is local time and 'Resets in' counts down. Rolling windows with no fixed reset (SuperGrok) show no reset time.

panels.title: Gemini Pro (Antigravity) — pools and pace
panels.description: The buckets `agy -p /usage` reports. `5h` and `week` are read from the same Hydrogen / 3.8 Flash bucket, so they move together and neither is a cap on its own; `1w` is Gemini 4 Argon's separate weekly bucket. Antigravity publishes a remaining fraction, not a credit count, so these are percent. **Pace** is left % minus the % of the window already elapsed: positive is ahead of an even burn, negative is a bucket that empties before it resets — the same arithmetic `dispatch budget` prints.

panels.title: OrcaRouter free — shared bucket, Hy4 bucket, active rung
panels.description: The free package publishes **caps, never a balance**, so there is no gauge to draw and no remaining figure to trust: what you see is the limit itself. `shared` is the bucket every free model draws on; a model with its own bucket gets its own row (Hy4's allows more requests than the shared one). The rung — the cap tier — is set by the account's lifetime paid spend, which no endpoint exposes, so `Lifetime paid` is the operator-recorded reading the rung is computed from (`ORCA_LIFETIME_SPEND_USD`); raise it when the console shows a higher figure.

panels.title: Metered balances
panels.description: Cash left on the pay-as-you-go accounts. DeepSeek and Moonshot publish a balance directly. MiMo publishes none, so its figure is derived: a balance read from the Xiaomi console, less everything opencode has booked against the provider since — re-anchor with `usage_exporter.py anchor mimo <usd>` when you top up or it drifts.

panels.title: Quota reading freshness
panels.description: Age of the cached vendor reading per plan. The exporter re-polls upstream hourly; anything over 3 hours is ignored for routing and the local run-count proxy is used instead.

panels.title: OrcaRouter wallet — balance against anchor and floor
panels.description: The wallet's dollar balance over time, with the operator-recorded anchor it started from and the **$2.00 floor** below which a paid run is refused. A line that only falls means every paid OrcaRouter dispatch is being charged to cash; the distance from the anchor is spend, the distance to the floor is how many paid runs are left.

panels.title: OrcaRouter wallet — now
panels.description: Balance, the anchor it is measured from, what has been spent since, and the floor that stops paid dispatches. `Spent since anchor` comes from OrcaRouter's own workspace spend quota, so it also counts spend from other clients on the same key — it can exceed what the registry booked.

panels.title: Quota burn-down and reset
panels.description: Credits left in each Z.ai pool over time. The sawtooth is the pool resetting; a line heading for zero before its reset is the cue to move work to another plan.

panels.title: New tokens by tier
panels.description: Tokens each tier actually had to ingest or generate, normalised per harness — codex reports input inclusive of its cached prefix while opencode and grok report cache separately, so raw counts are not comparable.

panels.title: Spent in cash (7d)
panels.description: Real money across every metered tier in the dashboard window.

panels.title: Avoided by prepaid (7d)
panels.description: What the prepaid tiers' tokens would have cost at the cheapest metered equivalent's list price. This is the subscriptions earning their keep.

panels.title: Dispatches (7d)
panels.description: Worker dispatches recorded across all tiers.

panels.title: Accept rate (7d)
panels.description: Share of reviewed dispatches accepted. Routing ranks on cost per ACCEPTED slice, so this is the denominator that matters — a cheap tier rejected half the time is the expensive one.

panels.title: Per-tier ledger — the numbers routing actually reads
panels.description: Cumulative per tier. Cost per accepted slice is the figure `auto` ranks on once a tier has enough judged runs; until then it falls back to priors. This table is also the accessible view of the panels above.

panels.title: Metered spend to date — including MiMo
panels.description: Cumulative cash per metered plan. MiMo is purely pay-as-you-go and is charged like DeepSeek and Kimi; it is here rather than in the balances panel only because Xiaomi publishes no balance endpoint to read.

panels.title: Windows that are biting
panels.description: Each window the provider itself reports as active, with its severity. A line at 100% means that plan's included usage is gone — for Claude Pro and Codex that is the orchestrator's own budget, not a worker's.

panels.title: Extra usage — money spent past the plan
panels.description: Once a window hits 100%, work bills against a monthly extra-usage cap rather than stopping. This is real money. The orchestrator's rule is to STOP and offer the choice at that point — never to continue silently, and never to refuse a decision that is the operator's.

panels.title: What this dashboard can and cannot see

options.content:
**Quota is the vendor's own number.** Z.ai publishes both Coding Plan pools (5-hour and weekly credits); Alibaba TP publishes a monthly credit pool; Anthropic publishes Claude Pro's 5-hour and 7-day utilisation, the same source Claude Code's own `/usage` reads; OpenAI publishes ChatGPT Plus / Codex's 5-hour and 7-day utilisation; OpenCode Go publishes 5-hour, weekly and monthly percent of the subscription from `inference/go/v1/usage`; and DeepSeek and Moonshot publish dollar balances. Polled hourly by a background refresher and served from cache; a reading older than 3 hours is ignored for routing.

**Gemini Pro (Antigravity) is read through `agy -p /usage`.** It reports its buckets as remaining *fractions*, so those pools are percent: `5h` and `week` are the same Hydrogen / 3.8 Flash bucket seen at two grains, and `1w` is Gemini 4 Argon's own weekly bucket. The pace column is left % minus the % of the window already elapsed — positive is ahead of an even burn, negative is a bucket that runs dry before it resets.

**OrcaRouter has two meters.** The wallet is a dollar balance from the workspace spend quota, with an operator-recorded anchor: *spent since anchor* is that anchor less the current balance, and a paid dispatch is refused below the **$2.00 floor**. The free package publishes caps, never a balance — one shared bucket plus a bucket for each free model that has its own (Hy4 does) — and the rung those caps sit on is set by the account's lifetime paid spend, which no endpoint exposes; it is an operator-recorded reading (`ORCA_LIFETIME_SPEND_USD`). There is deliberately no remaining gauge for the free lane: the vendor does not publish one, so drawing one would be a guess.

**MiMo's balance is derived, not published.** Xiaomi offers no balance endpoint, so the figure is an operator-recorded console reading less everything opencode has booked against the provider since. Re-anchor after a top-up.

**SuperGrok's figure costs a request.** xAI publishes no quota endpoint; the plan's headroom arrives as `x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining}-{tokens,requests}` on a chat response — the same numbers the CLI's `/usage` screen shows. The exporter reads it with a one-token completion, so it refreshes hourly rather than every 15 minutes.

**Cash is real; notional is modelled.** Prepaid tiers cost nothing at the margin, so *Avoided by prepaid* prices their tokens at the cheapest metered equivalent's list price. An estimate, not an invoice.

**Token counts are normalised per harness** — codex reports input inclusive of its cached prefix while opencode and grok report cache separately. Raw fields differ by roughly an order of magnitude and must not be compared directly.

**Seats come from the dispatch registry, not Prometheus history.** A seat's runs, verdicts, last-used time and lifetime spend survive a Prometheus restart; only the rate-shaped panels above need a full scrape window to be meaningful.

panels.title: P40 dispatches (7d)
panels.description: Worker runs on the thebrain Tesla P40 tiers (brain, brain-ornith, brain-dense).

panels.title: P40 accept rate, current seats (7d)
panels.description: Accepted at review / judged, P40 tiers.

panels.title: P40 tokens (7d)
panels.description: New tokens processed on the P40 (cache reads excluded).

panels.title: Value of free P40 work (7d)
panels.description: What the same tokens would cost on DeepSeek flash, the metered lane the P40 replaces.
